residual_risks: The diff touches docs/plans/2026-08-10-001-feat-tech-tree-icons-plan.md (readiness bumped requirements-only -> implementation-ready, new KD7/KD8, R4/R6 rewording) inside a branch whose stated intent is the shared-area-status feature plus a separately-authored farming drone. CLAUDE.md doesn't state an ownership rule for docs/plans/ files, so this isn't a quotable project-standards violation, but it is scope outside the stated intent and worth confirming with whoever owns that plan before merge.

GameActionPackGuards.ClassifyRefusal's updated doc comment (EcoServerMod/AdvancedElectronics/GameActionPackGuards.cs) now states outright that the refusal-classification call re-invokes ILawManager.Perform and applies any law effect that doesn't route through the pack's AccountChangeSet a second time -- a real-effect side effect on every classified refusal, on the mining drone's most-exercised world-write path. The comment says this is a known, deliberately-deferred defect rather than something this diff fixes, and no docs/solutions/ entry captures it, so it isn't currently a documented convention future changes can check against.

MiningExclusionEntry.SourceDockId and SurveyAreaEntry.ClaimHolderDockId both persist a dock's ObjectID as a string (matching the project's own established flat-primitive convention for [Serialized] classes), but neither this diff nor an existing docs/solutions/ entry states what happens to a claim or exclusion ledger entry whose owning dock is later deleted/picked up -- worth confirming the stale-holder-id path is exercised, since CONCEPTS.md's Drone Dock section says picking up a dock discards its own areas but says nothing about entries other docks hold referencing it.
testing_gaps: SurveyComponent.ChangeAreaKind's mid-pass refusal (EcoServerMod/AdvancedElectronics/SurveyComponent.cs) and DroneLifecycle.CurrentTargetArea's new DroneJobKind.Farm branch (EcoServerMod/AdvancedElectronics/DroneLifecycle.cs) are Eco-coupled glue -- the class of code docs/solutions/logic-errors/a-recovery-path-that-cannot-fire-in-the-state-it-exists-for.md documents as unreachable from EcoServerMod/AdvancedElectronics.Navigation.Tests and confirmable only by live testing. The pure-logic halves (AreaClaims, AreaOverlap, AreaLifecycle, AreaEdit) are well covered by the new *Tests.cs files, but the Eco-side wiring that calls them (assignment locking under AreaClaimLock, the farm-vs-mining GroundWriteAttribution handoff two independently-developed features now share) has no equivalent automated coverage.
